declaration.workload: one seed declares every workload: each engine and tier drives the identical load-then-run operation sequence the seeded generator emits, so driver differences never leak into workload semantics
declaration.elena_mapping: one key is one trajectory (namespace bench, session traj-<key>); an update appends the trajectory's next event; a read is the single-event read of the latest acknowledged event. The elena data set grows monotonically — an update is a new event, never an in-place overwrite — while the KV engines overwrite in place; that difference is elena's append-only semantics, declared here rather than hidden

tiers.configuration: every append fdatasync'ed to the data file before it acknowledges (elena.WithSyncAlways, the store default)
appends acknowledge after the write; a background flusher fdatasyncs the active data file once per 10ms (elena.WithSyncInterval; the final flush is forced at close and at every rotation)
every append commits as its own write transaction under bbolt's default sync-on-commit (Options.NoSync left false)
bbolt exposes no periodic-sync configuration (NoSync only turns syncing off), so this tier produces no bbolt numbers
SyncWrites set to true: badger msyncs the write-ahead value log after every write, the tier its option documentation scopes as surviving hard reboots (the v4 default is false; set explicitly)
badger exposes no periodic-sync configuration (SyncWrites false drops to plain mmap writes), so this tier produces no badger numbers

every append runs as one batch with Sync=true, whose commit fsyncs the write-ahead log before it acknowledges (the DB-level Sync flag stays false — in rosedb v2 it governs a write-ahead path the batch operations never ride, and it disables the batch-level sync)
rosedb's BytesPerSync flushes by accumulated bytes rather than by a time period, which is not this tier, so it produces no rosedb numbers
